budget.bus_pass.01.story: A new month begins. A monthly bus pass costs ₹400. Autos cost about ₹25 a trip, so ₹500 or more for the month. A friend says you can ride with him some days.
budget.bus_pass.01.a.label: Buy the monthly pass
budget.bus_pass.01.a.lesson: Paying once for the month can cost less than paying bit by bit.
budget.bus_pass.01.b.label: Pay for autos each day
budget.bus_pass.01.b.later: Auto fares added up. These two weeks cost ₹200 more.
budget.bus_pass.01.b.later2: More auto rides this week. Another ₹150 is gone.
budget.bus_pass.01.b.lesson: Small daily costs add up fast. Plan regular costs at the start of the month.
budget.bus_pass.01.c.label: Ride with a friend, free
budget.bus_pass.01.c.later: Your friend could not give a ride some days. Autos cost ₹150.
budget.bus_pass.01.c.lesson: A free plan can work, but it can break. Keep a back-up for the days it does.
budget.festival.01.story: Eid is next week. Laad Bazaar near Charminar is full of colour. A lovely festival kurta costs ₹200, and you are also saving for your goal.
budget.festival.01.a.label: Buy it from your Wants jar
budget.festival.01.a.lesson: Festivals are a good use of the Wants jar. Just check the price first.
budget.festival.01.b.label: Pick a ₹120 kurta, save ₹80
budget.festival.01.b.lesson: You still celebrate, and the ₹80 you did not spend moves your goal forward.
budget.festival.01.c.label: Buy on shop credit, pay later
budget.festival.01.c.later: The shopkeeper asks ₹240 today: the price plus extra for waiting.
budget.festival.01.c.lesson: Paying later often costs more. A plan made before the festival avoids this.
budget.friend_treat.01.story: It is your friend's birthday. The group wants to eat at a biryani place near Charminar. Each person pays ₹150.
budget.friend_treat.01.a.label: Pay your ₹150 share
budget.friend_treat.01.a.lesson: This is what the Wants jar is for. Planned fun is good fun.
budget.friend_treat.01.b.label: Suggest chai and samosas, ₹60
budget.friend_treat.01.b.lesson: A cheaper plan can still be a lovely treat. The time together is the gift.
budget.friend_treat.01.c.label: Borrow ₹300 and pay for all
budget.friend_treat.01.c.later: You pay back ₹350 for the ₹300 you borrowed. Your Wants jar feels empty.
budget.friend_treat.01.c.lesson: A treat paid with borrowed money costs more later. Treat within your budget.
budget.goal.01.story: Your goal is written on a paper inside your cupboard. Payday is here. Do you put money towards it first, or see what is left at month end?
budget.goal.01.a.label: Move ₹100 to the goal first
budget.goal.01.a.lesson: Pay your goal first, like a bill. What is left is yours to spend.
budget.goal.01.b.label: See what is left at month end
budget.goal.01.b.later: At month end, nothing was left. The goal did not move this month.
budget.goal.01.b.lesson: Money without a plan tends to disappear. A plan makes the goal real.
budget.goal.01.c.label: Start with ₹30, raise it later
budget.goal.01.c.lesson: A small start beats no start. Raise the amount when you can.
budget.recharge.01.story: Your phone recharge ends today. The shop near the bus stop has a ₹199 plan. Next to it, shiny earphones are on offer for ₹299.
budget.recharge.01.a.label: Just the ₹199 recharge
budget.recharge.01.a.lesson: Needs come first. Pay for what you must have before what you would like.
budget.recharge.01.b.label: Recharge and the earphones
budget.recharge.01.b.later: The cheap earphones stopped working. A new pair costs ₹150.
budget.recharge.01.b.lesson: Cheap wants can cost twice. Ask: will I still want this next week?
budget.recharge.01.c.label: Recharge now, save ₹100 for later
budget.recharge.01.c.lesson: Waiting lets you check if you still want it. Meanwhile, your ₹100 is safe.
budget.split.01.story: A cousin pays back the ₹300 you lent her last month. What a nice surprise! Now, where should this money go?
budget.split.01.a.label: ₹120 goal, ₹120 savings, ₹60 fun
budget.split.01.a.lesson: A simple split gives every jar a share, so the plan feels fair and easy.
budget.split.01.b.label: Put it all in Wants
budget.split.01.b.later: The extra ₹300 was gone in two weeks, mostly on small things.
budget.split.01.b.lesson: Money in the Wants jar goes fast. Decide where it goes before it arrives.
budget.split.01.c.label: Put it all towards the goal
budget.split.01.c.lesson: Strong for your goal. Keep a little for fun too, so the plan is easy to follow.
save.account.01.story: You keep ₹300 in cash in a tin at home. A parent says a bank savings account is safer, and it pays a little interest. A parent can help you open one.
save.account.01.a.label: Put it in a savings account
save.account.01.a.later: Six weeks on, the account has added about ₹1 of interest. Small, but you did nothing for it.
save.account.01.a.lesson: Interest is a small reward for keeping money in an account. The amount can change.
save.account.01.b.label: Keep it all in the tin
save.account.01.b.later: The tin was opened for small needs. ₹100 is gone.
save.account.01.b.lesson: Cash at home is easy to spend and can be lost. It earns no interest.
save.account.01.c.label: ₹100 in the tin, ₹200 in the account
save.account.01.c.later: Six weeks on, the ₹200 in the account has earned less than ₹1. The tin earned nothing.
save.account.01.c.lesson: A little cash for quick needs is fine. Keep most of your savings out of reach.
save.borrow.01.story: You need ₹300 for a school project kit by Friday, and your jars are low. A cousin offers to lend it. A stranger on WhatsApp also offers: 'Take it now, pay back ₹400 next week.'
save.borrow.01.a.label: Borrow from your cousin, set a date
save.borrow.01.a.later: You pay your cousin back ₹300, as you promised. Trust grows.
save.borrow.01.a.lesson: Borrow only what you need, from someone you trust, with a payback date.
save.borrow.01.b.label: Take the stranger's money
save.borrow.01.b.later: The stranger wants ₹400 next week, ₹100 extra, and keeps messaging you.
save.borrow.01.b.lesson: Interest is the extra you pay for borrowing. Always ask: how much will I pay back?
save.borrow.01.c.label: Share one kit with a classmate
save.borrow.01.c.lesson: Sharing the cost means you borrow nothing. Ask if the project allows it.
save.emergency.01.story: Your teacher says: keep a little 'rainy day' money for surprises. A repair or a medicine bill can come any week. You could start with ₹100.
save.emergency.01.a.label: Move ₹100 to Savings now
save.emergency.01.a.lesson: An emergency fund is money kept aside for surprises, so they do not hurt as much.
save.emergency.01.b.label: Start next month
save.emergency.01.b.lesson: Starting later is okay, but surprises do not wait. Even ₹20 helps today.
save.emergency.01.c.label: Keep it in my pocket, just in case
save.emergency.01.c.later: The pocket money slipped away on snacks and small things.
save.emergency.01.c.lesson: Money in your pocket is easy to spend. Keep emergency money in a separate place.
save.impulse.01.story: Sankranti is near. At a kite stall in the Old City, a pack of 10 fancy kites and string costs ₹250. You need two kites. The seller says: 'Last pack today!'
save.impulse.01.a.label: Buy just two kites, ₹60
save.impulse.01.a.lesson: Buy what you planned. 'Last one today' is a pressure trick.
save.impulse.01.b.label: Buy the full pack, ₹250
save.impulse.01.b.later: Most kites are still in the box. That ₹250 could have gone to your goal.
save.impulse.01.b.lesson: Pressure to buy now can make you spend more than you planned.
save.impulse.01.c.label: Wait a day, then decide
save.impulse.01.c.lesson: Waiting a day is a good test. If you still want it, buy only what you need.
save.rainy_day.01.story: A family member has a fever and needs a doctor and medicines. It costs ₹200. You remember the rainy-day money you started saving.
save.rainy_day.01.a.label: Use the rainy-day savings
save.rainy_day.01.a.later: You top up your rainy-day fund with ₹100 from this month.
save.rainy_day.01.a.lesson: This is exactly what the fund is for. Now try to fill it up again.
save.rainy_day.01.b.label: Ask a neighbour to lend ₹200
save.rainy_day.01.b.later: You give the ₹200 back to your neighbour. Your Needs jar feels tight.
save.rainy_day.01.b.lesson: A loan from someone you trust can help. It still has to be paid back.
save.rainy_day.01.c.label: Wait and see if it passes
save.rainy_day.01.c.later: The fever got worse. The next visit and tests cost ₹350.
save.rainy_day.01.c.lesson: Health cannot wait. This is the moment emergency savings is made for.
save.track.01.story: It is the 12th and your Wants jar is almost empty. Where did the money go? You cannot remember.
save.track.01.a.label: Write down every spend for a week
save.track.01.a.later: Your notes show tiny snack buys adding up. You skip them and move the ₹50 you did not spend from Wants to Savings.
save.track.01.a.lesson: Writing spends down shows where money goes. Then you can choose what to change.
save.track.01.b.label: Guess and hope for the best
save.track.01.b.later: Without notes, small buys kept adding up: ₹80 more.
save.track.01.b.lesson: Guessing misses the small things. Small things are often where money hides.
save.track.01.c.label: Check receipts and phone history
save.track.01.c.later: Receipts and phone history show some extra buys. You skip them and move ₹30 from Wants to Savings.
save.track.01.c.lesson: Receipts help, but they miss cash buys. A daily note covers everything.
invest.compound.01.story: Time Machine: ₹100 a month for 10 years is ₹12,000 put in. At assumed rates of {{lowRate}}% to {{highRate}}% a year, it could end near ₹{{low}}, ₹{{avg}} or ₹{{high}}. Nothing is promised.
invest.compound.01.a.label: Start ₹100 a month now
invest.compound.01.a.later: In this story, your first ₹100 grew to about ₹101 in six weeks. Tiny now, but growth builds on growth over years.
invest.compound.01.a.lesson: More time lets growth earn more growth. This is compounding. Rates here are assumed.
invest.compound.01.b.label: Start in 5 years, same ₹100
invest.compound.01.b.lesson: Waiting 5 years leaves less time, so it could end near ₹{{low}}, ₹{{avg}} or ₹{{high}}. Rates are assumed.
invest.compound.01.c.label: Put ₹100 in Rocket Co to double it
invest.compound.01.c.later: In this story, Rocket Co dipped: ₹100 became about ₹70. It might also have jumped.
invest.compound.01.c.lesson: Hoping to double fast is a gamble. Time can work better than luck.
invest.diversify.01.story: Basket Builder: place 10 coins of ₹10. In a bad year, Rocket Co might lose half and Mixed Basket a tenth. Rocket Co could also double in a good year. Steady Deposit grows slowly.
invest.diversify.01.a.label: All 10 coins in Rocket Co
invest.diversify.01.a.later: Skip ahead one bad year: Rocket Co lost half, so ₹100 is now ₹50. A good year could have gone the other way.
invest.diversify.01.a.lesson: All coins in one place means one bad year hits everything.
invest.diversify.01.b.label: Spread coins: 5, 3 and 2
invest.diversify.01.b.later: Skip ahead one bad year: ₹50 in Steady Deposit became ₹53, ₹30 in Mixed Basket ₹27, ₹20 in Rocket Co ₹10. Total ₹90, a smaller dip.
invest.diversify.01.b.lesson: Spreading coins can make a bad year hurt less. It does not remove risk.
invest.diversify.01.c.label: All 10 coins in Steady Deposit
invest.diversify.01.c.later: Skip ahead one bad year: ₹100 in Steady Deposit became about ₹106. In a good year, others might have gained more.
invest.diversify.01.c.lesson: Calm, but it might grow slowly. Every choice trades growth for comfort.
invest.hot_tip.01.story: A classmate forwards a message: 'Rocket Co will DOUBLE next month! Put in ₹300 now. Tell no one.' He says many others are already in.
invest.hot_tip.01.a.label: Ask who gains, then skip it
invest.hot_tip.01.a.lesson: Be careful with tips and 'tell no one'. Nobody can know the future.
invest.hot_tip.01.b.label: Put in ₹300 now
invest.hot_tip.01.b.later: In this story, Rocket Co fell. Your ₹300 is now about ₹120. It could have gone up, but nobody knew.
invest.hot_tip.01.b.lesson: A tip is a guess, not a plan. Money put in with a rush can drop.
invest.hot_tip.01.c.label: Try ₹50 just to see
invest.hot_tip.01.c.later: In this story, ₹50 became about ₹30. A small test cost little, but it was still a guess.
invest.hot_tip.01.c.lesson: A small amount limits the loss. It still treats a guess like a plan.
invest.inflation.01.story: Last year a plate of idli at the corner stall cost ₹40. Now it costs ₹42. Your ₹300 in a drawer buys a little less than before. This is inflation: prices slowly going up.
invest.inflation.01.a.label: Keep the ₹300 as cash at home
invest.inflation.01.a.later: Six weeks on, prices crept up a little. The ₹300 in the drawer is still ₹300, so it buys a bit less.
invest.inflation.01.a.lesson: Cash at home does not grow, so rising prices make it buy less over time.
invest.inflation.01.b.label: Put ₹300 in Steady Deposit
invest.inflation.01.b.later: In this story, ₹300 grew to about ₹302 in six weeks. That is slow, close to how fast prices rise. It might not always keep up.
invest.inflation.01.b.lesson: Money that grows might keep up better with rising prices. Nothing is promised.
invest.inflation.01.c.label: Spend all ₹300 today
invest.inflation.01.c.lesson: Spending early feels clever, but then nothing is left for later.
invest.loss.01.story: The Rocket Co money from the tip has fallen. Your classmate says: 'Put in ₹200 more! It will bounce back and you win it all back.'
invest.loss.01.a.label: Do not add more, learn from it
invest.loss.01.a.lesson: Adding more to win back a loss can make the loss bigger. Plan before you put money in.
invest.loss.01.b.label: Add ₹200 to win it back
invest.loss.01.b.later: In this story, Rocket Co fell again. The ₹200 is now about ₹90. Chasing a loss can deepen it.
invest.loss.01.b.lesson: A loss is not a reason to bet more. Rocket Co could rise or fall, nobody knows.
invest.loss.01.c.label: Ask a trusted adult first
invest.loss.01.c.lesson: Talking it over slows you down. Slow is good when money is on the line.
invest.risk.01.story: Game money: ₹300 is set aside for an exam fee due in 6 weeks. Three made-up places for it: Steady Deposit (slow and steady), Mixed Basket (a mix), Rocket Co (could jump or drop).
invest.risk.01.a.label: Steady Deposit
invest.risk.01.a.later: In this story, Steady Deposit grew a little: ₹300 became about ₹302. It might not always.
invest.risk.01.a.lesson: Money needed soon fits steady places better. Steady ones might grow slowly, though.
invest.risk.01.b.label: Mixed Basket
invest.risk.01.b.later: In this story, Mixed Basket dipped for a while: ₹300 became about ₹288. It could have gone up too.
invest.risk.01.b.lesson: A mix can soften big drops, but over a short time it can still dip.
invest.risk.01.c.label: Rocket Co
invest.risk.01.c.later: In this story, Rocket Co dropped: ₹300 became about ₹165. It could have jumped, but the fee was due now.
invest.risk.01.c.lesson: Rocket Co could jump, but it could also drop. With a short wait, a drop can hurt.
safe.job_fee.01.story: A poster at the college gate says: 'Data entry from home, ₹800 a day! Pay ₹500 registration first.' A senior says he joined. You could use extra money.
safe.job_fee.01.a.label: Walk away: real jobs charge no fee
safe.job_fee.01.a.lesson: A real job pays you. It does not ask you to pay first.
safe.job_fee.01.b.label: Pay ₹500 to register
safe.job_fee.01.b.later: The number is switched off. No work ever comes.
safe.job_fee.01.b.lesson: Fees to get a job are a common trick. Report on cybercrime.gov.in or call 1930.
safe.job_fee.01.c.label: Ask the college office or a teacher
safe.job_fee.01.c.lesson: Asking adults you trust before paying is always a good step.
safe.loan_app.01.story: Friends plan a weekend outing that costs ₹1,000. A phone ad says: 'Instant loan in 2 minutes. No papers, no questions!' You are tempted.
safe.loan_app.01.a.label: Take the instant loan
safe.loan_app.01.a.later: The app asks ₹1,400: your ₹1,000 plus ₹400 in fees and interest. Calls start if you are late.
safe.loan_app.01.a.lesson: Instant loan apps can charge very high fees. A loan must be paid back, with extra.
safe.loan_app.01.b.label: Plan a ₹200 picnic with home food
safe.loan_app.01.b.lesson: You can have fun while spending only what you have.
safe.loan_app.01.c.label: Skip it this time
safe.loan_app.01.c.lesson: Saying no today keeps your money free for your goal.
safe.lottery.01.story: A WhatsApp message from an unknown number says: 'You won ₹10,00,000 in the Lucky Draw! Pay ₹200 today for your claim code.' You never entered any draw.
safe.lottery.01.a.label: Delete, block and tell someone
safe.lottery.01.a.lesson: You cannot win a draw you never entered. Real prizes never ask for a fee first.
safe.lottery.01.b.label: Pay ₹200 to claim the prize
safe.lottery.01.b.later: A new message: 'Pay ₹1,500 more for tax.' The prize never comes.
safe.lottery.01.b.lesson: Scammers ask for a small fee, then more. Report on 1930 or cybercrime.gov.in.
safe.lottery.01.c.label: Reply to ask if it is real
safe.lottery.01.c.later: Your number starts getting more scam messages and calls.
safe.lottery.01.c.lesson: Replying tells scammers your number is active. Delete and block instead.
safe.otp.01.story: A caller says he is from your bank. 'Your account will be blocked! Tell me the OTP (a one-time code sent by SMS) we just sent, quickly!'
safe.otp.01.a.label: Hang up and share nothing
safe.otp.01.a.lesson: A real bank never asks for your OTP. It is like a key: never share it.
safe.otp.01.b.label: Read out the OTP
safe.otp.01.b.lesson: An OTP lets others take your money. Never share it. If it happens, call 1930 fast.
safe.otp.01.c.label: Say 'I will call the bank myself'
safe.otp.01.c.lesson: Calling the number on your bank card is safe. Never use a number the caller gives.
safe.report.01.story: You shared your OTP and ₹400 left your account. You feel worried. This happens to many people, even careful ones. What do you do now?
safe.report.01.a.label: Call 1930 and tell an adult now
safe.report.01.a.later: Because you reported fast, part of the money came back in this story: ₹200.
safe.report.01.a.lesson: Report fast on 1930 or cybercrime.gov.in. Getting tricked is not your fault.
safe.report.01.b.label: Say nothing, feeling embarrassed
safe.report.01.b.later: Two days later, the same caller tries again with a new story.
safe.report.01.b.lesson: Staying quiet helps scammers. Telling someone early gives the best chance to limit the loss.
safe.report.01.c.label: Call the 'refund' number in an SMS
safe.report.01.c.lesson: Fake refund numbers are a second trick. Use only official numbers, like 1930.
safe.upi_collect.01.story: You offer your old school bag for sale. A buyer says: 'Approve my UPI (phone money) collect request. Enter your PIN to receive ₹300.'
safe.upi_collect.01.a.label: Ignore it: no PIN to receive
safe.upi_collect.01.a.lesson: You never need a PIN to receive money. A PIN is only for sending money.
safe.upi_collect.01.b.label: Enter the PIN to get the money
safe.upi_collect.01.b.lesson: A collect request pulls money out of you. Entering a PIN approves it.
safe.upi_collect.01.c.label: Offer to meet and be paid in person
safe.upi_collect.01.c.lesson: Meeting in a public place with an adult is safer. Check the cash before handing over.
event.bicycle_puncture.01.story: The tyre of your bicycle goes flat on the way to college. The roadside shop fixes it for ₹50.
event.bicycle_puncture.01.lesson: Small surprises add up. A little rainy-day money takes the stress away.
event.bonus_tip.01.story: A customer likes your quick, friendly service and gives you a ₹100 tip.
event.bonus_tip.01.lesson: Extra money is a chance: some for savings, some for fun.
event.exam_fee.01.story: The college says the exam fee of ₹500 is due two weeks earlier than you thought.
event.exam_fee.01.a.label: Pay it now from savings
event.exam_fee.01.a.lesson: Savings help when dates move. This is why we keep some aside.
event.exam_fee.01.b.label: Pay from your goal money
event.exam_fee.01.b.lesson: It works, but your goal moves further away. Savings come first for surprises.
event.exam_fee.01.c.label: Pay late and add a ₹100 fine
event.exam_fee.01.c.later: You paid late: the ₹500 fee plus a ₹100 fine.
event.exam_fee.01.c.lesson: Paying late often costs extra. Know your due dates in advance.
event.festival_gift.01.story: It is Diwali. Relatives give you ₹300 as a festival gift. What a lovely surprise!
event.festival_gift.01.a.label: Save half, enjoy half
event.festival_gift.01.a.lesson: Extra money is a chance to save first, then enjoy.
event.festival_gift.01.b.label: Keep it all for fun
event.festival_gift.01.b.lesson: Enjoy it, and notice how fast it goes. Save a little next time.
event.festival_gift.01.c.label: Put it all towards the goal
event.festival_gift.01.c.lesson: Strong for your goal. Keep a little for fun so you stay on track.
event.friend_borrow.01.story: A friend asks to borrow ₹100 until Friday. They say they will pay you back.
event.friend_borrow.01.a.label: Lend all ₹100
event.friend_borrow.01.a.later: Your friend paid back ₹50 so far and says the rest comes soon.
event.friend_borrow.01.a.lesson: Lend only money you can live without. Loans are not always paid back on time.
event.friend_borrow.01.b.label: Give ₹30 as a gift, not a loan
event.friend_borrow.01.b.lesson: A small gift you will not miss keeps the friendship free of stress.
event.friend_borrow.01.c.label: Say kindly: 'Not this time'
event.friend_borrow.01.c.lesson: It is okay to say no. A good friend understands.
event.hospital.01.story: A family member has a high fever. The clinic visit and medicines cost ₹300 this week.
event.hospital.01.a.label: Pay from savings
event.hospital.01.a.lesson: Health comes first. A little savings makes hard days easier.
event.hospital.01.b.label: Ask a relative to lend ₹300
event.hospital.01.b.later: You give the ₹300 back to your relative this month.
event.hospital.01.b.lesson: A loan from family can help. It still has to be paid back.
event.hospital.01.c.label: Wait and see if it passes
event.hospital.01.c.later: The fever got worse. The next visit and tests cost ₹600.
event.hospital.01.c.lesson: Some things cannot wait. This is why an emergency fund matters.
event.prices_rise.01.story: Vegetables, oil and rice cost more this month. Your daily costs go up by about ₹100.
event.prices_rise.01.a.label: Cut a want to cover it
event.prices_rise.01.a.lesson: When prices rise, look at wants first. Needs come first.
event.prices_rise.01.b.label: Pay the extra from savings
event.prices_rise.01.b.lesson: Savings can help once. If prices stay high, you need a new plan.
event.prices_rise.01.c.label: Buy on shop credit
event.prices_rise.01.c.later: The shop asks ₹120 for the ₹100 of goods you took on credit.
event.prices_rise.01.c.lesson: Credit can cost extra. A small tweak in your plan costs less.
event.rain_stock.01.story: Heavy rain soaks the stall's vegetables and about ₹300 of stock is wasted. Your father looks worried.
event.rain_stock.01.a.label: Cover ₹300 from your savings
event.rain_stock.01.a.later: Heavy rain again. With no cover, another ₹300 of stock was wasted, and your savings paid again.
event.rain_stock.01.a.lesson: Helping family in a hard week is kind. Savings make it possible without stress.
event.rain_stock.01.b.label: Cover it from your bike money
event.rain_stock.01.b.later: Heavy rain again. With no cover, another ₹300 of stock was wasted. It came from your bike money again.
event.rain_stock.01.b.lesson: It can be done, but your bike goal moves further away.
event.rain_stock.01.c.label: Cover ₹300, buy a ₹150 cover sheet
event.rain_stock.01.c.later: Heavy rain again, but the cover sheet kept the stock dry. No new ₹300 loss this time.
event.rain_stock.01.c.lesson: Small prevention can cost less than a big loss. Plan for what you can predict.
event.screen_crack.01.story: Your phone slips from your hand and the screen cracks. A proper repair costs ₹800.
event.screen_crack.01.a.label: Pay for the repair from savings
event.screen_crack.01.a.lesson: This is what an emergency fund is for: surprises that cannot wait.
event.screen_crack.01.b.label: Put on a cheap screen guard for now
event.screen_crack.01.b.later: The crack spread, and the full repair now costs ₹900.
event.screen_crack.01.b.lesson: A cheap fix can buy time, but the real repair may cost more later.
event.screen_crack.01.c.label: Ask two shops, pay ₹550
event.screen_crack.01.c.lesson: Comparing prices can save money. Savings made it possible to act fast.
event.slow_week.01.story: A slow week: fewer people need your work. You earn about ₹300 less than usual, but your costs stay the same.
event.slow_week.01.a.label: Cover the gap from savings
event.slow_week.01.a.lesson: Irregular income has slow weeks. Savings from busy weeks smooth them out.
event.slow_week.01.b.label: Skip treats, use ₹300 of Wants
event.slow_week.01.b.lesson: Cutting wants for a week is a fair plan. Do not let it become a habit of zero fun.
event.slow_week.01.c.label: Borrow ₹300 until next week
event.slow_week.01.c.later: You repay the ₹300 next week, and it takes from next week's money.
event.slow_week.01.c.lesson: Short borrowing can work, but it eats next week's money and starts a cycle.
quiz.budget.needs.baseline.q: Which of these is a need?
quiz.budget.needs.baseline.why: A need is something you must have, like getting to college.
quiz.budget.plan.baseline.q: Payday has come. Which habit helps your goal most?
quiz.budget.plan.baseline.o1: Spend first, save what is left
quiz.budget.plan.baseline.o2: Move money to your goal first
quiz.budget.plan.baseline.why: Paying your goal first, like a bill, makes sure it happens.
quiz.save.emergency.baseline.q: What is an emergency fund for?
quiz.save.emergency.baseline.why: An emergency fund covers costs you did not plan for.
quiz.invest.compound.baseline.q: ₹500 a month might grow more over the years because…
quiz.invest.compound.baseline.why: Compounding: what your money earns can earn more too. Results are never promised.
quiz.safe.otp.baseline.q: Who should you share your OTP with?
quiz.safe.otp.baseline.why: Never share an OTP, not even with someone who says they are from a bank.
quiz.safe.collect.baseline.q: To receive money by UPI, you need to…
quiz.safe.collect.baseline.o2: Do nothing: no PIN is needed to receive
quiz.safe.collect.baseline.why: You never need a PIN to receive money. A PIN is only for sending.
quiz.budget.needs.endline.q: Which one counts as a need?
quiz.budget.needs.endline.why: A need is something your health or studies depend on, like medicine.
quiz.budget.plan.endline.q: You want to reach a ₹3,000 goal. What is the best first step with this month's pay?
quiz.budget.plan.endline.o1: Set some aside as soon as pay comes
quiz.budget.plan.endline.o2: See what is left at month end
quiz.budget.plan.endline.why: Setting money aside first turns a wish into a plan.
quiz.save.emergency.endline.q: Your phone breaks suddenly. Which money do you use first?
quiz.save.emergency.endline.o3: A loan from a stranger's app
quiz.save.emergency.endline.why: Rainy-day savings are made for surprises, so your goal stays safe.
quiz.invest.compound.endline.q: Why might starting early help money grow more?
quiz.invest.compound.endline.o3: Growth has more time to build on growth
quiz.invest.compound.endline.why: More time lets growth build on growth. Rates change, and nothing is promised.
quiz.safe.otp.endline.q: A caller says he is from the bank and asks for the code you just got by SMS. You…
quiz.safe.otp.endline.why: A real bank never asks for your OTP. Hang up. Call 1930 if money was lost.
quiz.safe.collect.endline.q: A buyer sends a collect request and says 'approve with your PIN to get paid'. What is true?
quiz.safe.collect.endline.o1: Approving with a PIN sends money out
quiz.safe.collect.endline.o3: The PIN only checks the buyer is real
quiz.safe.collect.endline.why: A collect request pulls money from you. Approving it with a PIN pays the other person.
scam.kyc_link.01.s1: Dear customer, your account will be BLOCKED today.
scam.why.urgency: Pressure to act right now is a warning sign.
scam.why.link: Unknown links can steal your details.
scam.kyc_link.01.why: Real banks never ask you to update KYC (proof of who you are) through an SMS link. Report on 1930.
scam.otp_call.01.s1: Hello, I am calling from your bank's head office.
scam.why.unknown_sender: You do not know this sender. Be careful.
scam.otp_call.01.s2: A code just reached your phone. Read it to me.
scam.why.asks_otp: No honest person asks for your OTP.
scam.otp_call.01.s3: I need it within one minute or your card stops.
scam.otp_call.01.why: Banks never ask for an OTP on a call. Hang up. If money is lost, call 1930.
scam.lottery.01.s1: CONGRATULATIONS! You won ₹10,00,000 in our Lucky Draw!
scam.why.too_good: Too good to be true usually is.
scam.lottery.01.s2: Pay ₹200 for your claim code today to get the prize.
scam.why.upfront_fee: Real prizes never ask you to pay first.
scam.lottery.01.why: You cannot win a draw you never entered, and real prizes never ask for a fee.
scam.job_fee.01.s1: Work from home! Earn ₹800 a day with simple typing.
scam.job_fee.01.s2: Pay ₹500 registration fee to get your joining letter.
scam.why.job_fee: Real jobs pay you. They do not charge a fee.
scam.job_fee.01.why: Real employers pay you. They do not ask you to pay to get a job.
scam.collect.01.s1: Hi, I want your old bag. I sent a collect request of ₹500.
scam.why.collect: A collect request takes money out of your account.
scam.collect.01.s2: Please enter your UPI PIN to receive it.
scam.why.asks_pin: A PIN is only for sending money. Never share it.
scam.collect.01.why: You never need a PIN to receive money. A collect request takes money out.
scam.qr_receive.01.s1: Scan this QR to receive your ₹2,000 refund.
scam.why.qr_receive: Scanning a QR sends money out. You never scan to receive.
scam.qr_receive.01.s2: Then enter your PIN to confirm.
scam.qr_receive.01.why: Scanning a QR and entering a PIN sends money out. Receiving never needs a scan or a PIN.
scam.loan_app.01.s1: Instant loan up to ₹10,000 in 2 minutes. No papers!
scam.loan_app.01.why: This is a scam: real lenders check who you are and show the full cost first. "No papers" apps hide huge fees, copy your contacts and threaten you.
scam.betting.01.s1: Double your money in tonight's match! Join our group.
scam.betting.01.why: Betting is built so most people lose money. Doubling is the hook. Do not bet, do not click.
safe.exam_fee.01.s1: Exam fee is due on the 15th. Pay at the college counter and collect a receipt.
safe.exam_fee.01.why: No link, no OTP, and you pay in person with a receipt.
safe.otp_sms.01.s1: OTP 482913 is for the ₹400 bus pass payment you just started on the college fee page. Do not share it with anyone.
safe.otp_sms.01.why: You started this bus pass payment yourself a moment ago, and the message says not to share the code. It is a warning only if someone asks for it.
safe.family_call.01.s1: I sent ₹500 for your books. It will show in your account.
safe.family_call.01.s2: You do not need to do anything.
safe.family_call.01.why: It is a saved contact you know, and receiving money needs no PIN, OTP or scan.
safe.shop_qr.01.s1: Scan this board to pay ₹20 for chai. The shop name shows on your screen.
safe.shop_qr.01.why: You are paying a shop you can see, an amount you choose, and you can check the name. Paying is when you scan.
persona.sana.name: Sana
persona.sana.bio: Sana, 18, teaches tuition after college. She is the first in her family heading to a degree.
persona.ravi.name: Ravi
persona.ravi.bio: Ravi, 17, helps at his father's tiffin stall in the Old City. Sales go up at Ramzan, Bonalu, Dussehra and Diwali, and dip in quiet weeks.
reflection.save_first: Next month, try putting some money in Savings on payday, before you spend.
reflection.build_cushion: Next month, try to grow your Savings so one surprise bill will not hurt.
reflection.goal_steps: Next month, move a little to your goal on every payday. Small steps add up.
reflection.pay_down_debt: Next month, try to pay back a little of what you borrowed.
reflection.great_month: Great month! Your plan is working. Keep the same habits going.
assumption.banner: These are assumed numbers, not promises. Real results can be higher or lower.
